_comment: Jackson Roofing (Chris Jackson, Plano TX). WIN-BACK PITCH, rebuilt 2026-09-06 on top of the dashboard published 2026-08-28, so the same link keeps working and now carries the full record. HONESTY DECISIONS, all deliberate: (1) Seventeen blog posts total. FIVE were published 2026-09-06 to the rebuilt site repo (blog/*.html), read live off git history, and all five URLs were curl-verified 200 that day. The other TWELVE are REAL work published on jacksonroofingco.com during the engagement, reconciled 2026-09-06 against the content-engine state file (see history/jackson-roofing-legacy.json for the full reconciliation): one post was logged twice under the same URL and is now listed once at its first publish date, and a twelfth post that published with no URL recorded is listed as a non-linked row. Two non-blog rows from 2026-07-20 (a Google Business post and a round of review requests) are carried under their own types so they read as the actions they were. jacksonroofingco.com now Cloudflare-blocks our IP (403 from curl and from a real browser), so we CANNOT re-verify those URLs today and this page never claims we did. They carry their real 2026-07 and 2026-08 dates and sit under a group that names the period, so nothing reads as work happening now. Chris can open every one of them from his own network. (2) Every wingdigital26-maker.github.io link on this page was curl-verified 200 on 2026-09-06. (3) Between 2026-08-28 and 2026-09-06 nothing published, and the September bar in the chart carries only the five posts from 2026-09-06. No weekly cadence, Google posting or emailing is running today, and the banner and subhead both say so rather than letting five posts read as a live program. (4) No traffic, ranking, call, lead or revenue number appears anywhere; pendingMetrics records why for each one. (5) The one measured fact we hold on this account is that social produced no leads, and the social card says exactly that instead of selling social. GoHighLevel is retired and is referenced nowhere in this file. No em dashes or en dashes in any client-facing string.
_brand_comment: Site shown as plain text, not a link: jacksonroofingco.com Cloudflare-blocks our IP so we cannot verify it from here, and an unverified link is worse than none. Headline leads with the referral list because that is the asset that has never been used. Rebuilt-site showcase and the month-by-month plan were both cut by Jack on 2026-09-06.

The template pins itself to the light ground by design, so the light accent is the deeper #06809f for readable contrast on white, while the badge keeps the real black-plate-and-cyan pairing.
_types_comment: core and blog are the only types with real items, so they are the only keys, bars and counts the template can draw. service and city are declared so their colors stay stable the moment those pages are real; with no items they render nothing at all, which is why this page can never show a fabricated zero.
_referralPartners_comment: The referral partner asset. Sourced live at build time from ghl-cli/jackson_roofing_leads.db (table leads), so every number on the page is a straight count of rows and nothing is transcribed by hand. HONESTY DECISIONS: (1) emailMask is on, so build.py part hides every address before it reaches the HTML. A texted dashboard link is effectively public and 460 harvestable business addresses must not be published; Chris gets the full file directly. (2) hiddenCategories drops insurance-adjuster (151 rows) from the VISIBLE category breakdown while keeping it inside the headline total, because Texas Insurance Code Chapter 4102 restricts roofers acting as public adjusters and roofer to adjuster outreach is legally sensitive. hidden_note says so on the page, out loud, so the 869 visible plus 151 held back still adds to 1,020 for anyone who checks. Flip this key to an empty list to show them. (3) status is 'staged' on every row in the table, so the claim that nothing has been sent is literally true. (4) No response rate, conversion rate or revenue projection appears anywhere; none exists in the source.

referralPartners.title: Your outreach list
referralPartners.intro: Roofing work comes from people who run into a roof problem doing their own job. We built you a list of them across North Texas: general contractors, property managers, inspectors, restoration firms and HOA managers, enriched with real phone numbers, addresses and contacts.
referralPartners.sample_note: Real rows out of the list, shown as stored. Email addresses are part hidden on purpose: this page gets forwarded, and a page anyone can open holding hundreds of full business addresses is a list anyone can take. You get the complete unmasked file.
referralPartners.note: Real businesses, researched one by one and enriched from public sources.
referralPartners._exclude_comment: insurance-adjuster rows are dropped from the dataset entirely, not hidden inside the total. Texas Insurance Code Chapter 4102 restricts a roofer from acting as a public adjuster, so pitching adjuster outreach to a roofing client is not something to put in writing. Dropping them also makes every count on the page reconcile without a disclosure box.

_outreach_comment: Three cards, all honestly blocked on access, all phrased as forward plans rather than as excuses. Storm and hail targeting is deliberately NOT a card: it needs nothing from Chris, it needs the engagement to restart, so it lives in the plan instead of pretending to be a lane waiting on his login. The social card states the measured result rather than selling the channel.

channels.name: Review requests

channels.name: Facebook and Instagram
channels.note: Straight answer: we measured social for your account and it brought in no leads. We will keep the pages current so anyone checking you out sees a live business, but we are not going to tell you it is where the work comes from.

_reviewStanding_comment: Generic dashboard block. The figures live in history/jackson-review-gap.json, read live off the public Google listings on the pull date. The copy below is client-facing framing only; it states the standing and the gap and never predicts a result.

reviewStanding.title: Where you stand on Google reviews
reviewStanding.intro: Your Google profile next to twelve roofing contractors Google returns for Plano, Frisco, McKinney, Allen and Richardson. Every rating and count here was read off the live listings on the pull date.
reviewStanding.banner: Reviews carry roughly a fifth of local pack weight, second only to the profile itself, and they are the clearest lever on this list that is still open to you.

tiles: reviews between you and the median

reviewStanding.source_line: Source: Google Maps listings for Jackson Roofing and for the roofing contractors Google returns on the searches roofing contractor Plano, Frisco, McKinney, Allen and Richardson TX. Candidate list built with the same open source Google Maps scraper Wing uses for prospecting; every rating and count then read live on the listing itself.
reviewStanding.note: Your profile is live and complete on the basics: address, phone, website, hours, category and 6 photos. The gap is volume. The three reviews Google shows on the profile are 6, 7 and 8 years old, so the profile reads as quiet rather than as bad. Nothing on this page is a forecast: it is the standing as Google displayed it on the pull date, and the gap figures are subtraction.

_stormHistory_comment: Storm history section. Generic template block: build.py reads the data file named below and the template renders a section only because this key exists. Every number on the page is a count of records in NOAA's public Storm Events Database, pulled 2026-09-07 from https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/swdi/stormevents/csvfiles/. Nothing here is estimated, projected or inferred: NOAA does not record roofs damaged, homes affected or revenue, so no such figure appears. This is intelligence we can act on, not work already performed. Copy must stay factual and short.

stormHistory.title: Hail history in your service area
stormHistory.intro: Every hail report NOAA logged in Collin, Denton, Dallas, Rockwall and Kaufman counties over the 24 months from June 2024 through May 2026. These are recorded events, not estimates.
stormHistory.banner: Hail is the demand signal for residential roof replacement in North Texas. This is the record for your counties.

labels.monthLabel: What months the hail lands in
labels.cityLabel: Your cities named on the record

stormHistory.source_line: Source: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, Storm Events Database. Filters: Texas, counties Collin, Denton, Dallas, Rockwall and Kaufman, event type Hail, June 2024 through May 2026.
stormHistory.note: 1 inch is the size that typically damages asphalt shingles, which is why it is counted separately. We have not contacted anyone off this data or run any campaign from it. It is the targeting layer we would build on, and it is here so you can check it yourself.
